title: Canonical Reality preserves valid-time kind and source precision
failure_signature: A timeless Fact and an unknown-time Fact become indistinguishable at the canonical/read layer, or a month/quarter/range source is silently represented as a more precise occurrence than the source supports.
root_cause: Canonical Fact storage originally preserved nullable bounds and later precision text but not the semantic valid_time_kind; consumers could then infer semantics from NULL bounds or invent precision during replay.
invariant: Canonical Reality must carry valid_time_kind, bounds, precision and source time text as first-class inherited semantics. NULL bounds never determine timeless versus unknown, and replay must not manufacture a finer occurrence precision than the supporting source/assertion.
anti_regression: Do not infer timeless/unknown from `valid_from IS NULL AND valid_to IS NULL`.
Do not coerce month/quarter/range evidence into a fake exact day for convenience.
Do not let PostgreSQL and DuckDB drop different parts of the temporal extent.

guards.contains: ADD COLUMN valid_time_kind text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown'
guards.description: Canonical Fact schema stores valid-time kind explicitly.
Integrated hard gate checks kind, month precision and source time text on canonical Reality.

revisit_when: Only revisit if TemporalExtent is deliberately replaced by an equally explicit model that can distinguish period/timeless/unknown and round-trip source-supported precision without inference from missing bounds.
